title: Take a link out only when its host has stopped answering

blocks.text: This picks up where the previous practice ended: `LinkPolicy` already contains its solution, and the sign-on manager now also reports every echo to it.
Two incidents from the same month:

items: Every evening during the host's batch run, link A leaves the pool for a moment and signs on again, though nothing is wrong with the host. The manager takes a link out after a single unanswered echo.
A colleague's first fix counted unanswered echoes and took the link out at the third. On Friday a link that had missed one echo on Monday and one on Wednesday was taken out over a single slow answer.

blocks.text: The network's operations team settled on `echoLimit`: after that many unanswered echoes, the manager gives up on a link whose host has stopped answering. Finish `signedOn`, `echoAnswered` and `echoFailed` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/LinkPolicy.java`. About five lines in total.

cases.says: with a limit of 3, one unanswered echo leaves the link in the pool
a host that answers no echo at all is eventually reported as needing a new sign-on
an answered echo clears the failures before it, so failures spread out over time never reach the limit
the failure that reaches the limit asks for a new sign-on, not the one after it; a limit of 1 reacts to the first
failures counted before a new sign-on do not count against it

origin.section: 15.3 One Lost Echo Is Not a Dead Host

concepts: Only echo failures in a row count, an answered echo or a new sign-on starts the count again, and the link is taken out at the limit.
